newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine peso Letes seen sold at 7.5 pct yield.
newsitem.headline: Argentine peso Letes seen sold at 7.5 pct yield.

text.p: Argentina's auction Tuesday of 250 million pesos in 91-day treasury bills Letes is likely to fetch a cut-off yield of around 7.50 percent, analysts and traders said Monday.
They also estimated the sale of $500 million in 364-day bills are set to be sold at a cut-off yield of around seven percent.
"I think the whole auction should go off pretty well," said an analyst at a large foreign bank.
Estimates for the peso bill ranged from as low as 6.75 percent to as high as 7.75 percent.
The last time Argentina auctioned 91-day bills denominated in pesos, in August, there was a cut-off yield of 8.50 percent. Also in August, dollar bills maturing in 182 days were sold at 6.49 percent.
At last month's auction only 91-day dollar-denominated bills were sold and they fetched a cut-off yield of 6.10 percent.

Players said the market may pay more attention to the dollar issue Tuesday than the peso one because this is the first time since the government launched its Letes program at the beginning of the year that 364-day paper will be issued.
"Because this is the first time there are bills with a year's maturity, its not possible to say what kind of yield there will be," said the chief trader at an Argentine bank.
The longest maturity so far has been 182-day bills.

The analyst at the foreign bank pointed out that "people don't want to be in cash right now" because of the firm underlying tone in the bond market, meaning that investors may not want to commit large funds to bills. That means Tuesday's bill auction may be of less significance as a market indicator than usual.
Bids for the bills are due by 2 p.m. (1 p.m. EDT/1700 GMT). The issues will be settled on October 18.
The 91-day bills mature on January 17 and the 364-day bills mature on October 17, 1997.
